title: NoRecognition: AI Adversarial Clothing
text:
Extremely limited drop · First come, first served
Clothing the cameras cannot see.
A year of research becomes something you can wear. Presented on stage
 at Black Hat and DEF CON, and dropping at the same moment.

No obligation. Notified backers get in before the limited tiers are
 gone.
Same person. Same camera. Identical coverage on both sides, only the
 pattern changes. Real output from a production person detector.
A small run, and then it is gone.
Every piece is made to order and the limited tiers are capped. When
 they are taken, they are taken. There is no restock of a one of one.
Tee
The everyday piece. Torso coverage is the surface we have tested
 hardest.
Hoodie
Maximum coverage. The most pattern we can put on a person.
Buff
Small, loud, and the one people ask about. Neck gaiter, headband,
 or pulled up.
One of one
A pattern generated for a single person, validated, and never
 released, shown, or printed for anyone else. If the vendors ever
 train against our public prints, yours was never in the dataset.
50 of each. That is the whole run.
Everyone else asks you to trust them.
There is a whole category of anti surveillance clothing now, and
 almost none of it publishes a single test result. Every pattern here
 is scored before it ships, and the method is public.
Measured
Scored against eleven production computer vision models, including
 the vehicle and person detector running on tens of thousands of
 American streets.
Controlled
A pattern has to beat a plain panel of the same size. A big print
 that simply covers you does not count.
Held out
Scored on thirty test wearers that were never used to build
 it.
Honest
We publish the results that went against us too.
